extracted.intended_audience: Applicants, agents and industrial property offices filing or prosecuting ARIPO patent, utility model and industrial design applications (including biotech filings)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing filing, formal and substantive examination, fees, claims drafting, biotech exceptions, priority declarations, divisional and conversion requests under the Harare (ARIPO) Protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination of expert and undertaking (Rule 6bis.3(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The nomination shall be accompanied by an undertaking from the expert vis-à-vis the applicant similar to that specified in Rule 6bis.2(1); in this instance the requester will be regarded as a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: New deposit deemed no interruption (Rule 6bis.4(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a deposited micro-organism ceases to be available because it is no longer viable or the depository cannot supply samples, an interruption in availability shall be deemed not to have occurred if a new deposit of the originally deposited micro-organism is made within 3 months from the date the depositor was notified and a copy of the receipt is forwarded to the Office within 4 months from the date of the new deposit stating the application or ARIPO patent number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies where original deposit not transferred to another recognised depository; strict 3- and 4-month notification/receipt time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place of new deposit following interruption (Rule 6bis.4(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If unavailability is due to non-viability the new deposit shall be made with the same depository; if due to the depository being unable to supply, it may be made with another depository recognised for the purposes of Rule 6bis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement of 3-month period when depository ceases recognition (Rule 6bis.4(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original depository ceases to be recognised or discontinues functions and the notification is not received within 6 months of the event, the 3-month period begins on the date the event is announced in the Journal of the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of identity for new deposit (Rule 6bis.4(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new deposit shall be accompanied by a statement signed by the depositor alleging that the newly deposited micro-organism is the same as that originally deposited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must define protection sought in technical terms (Rule 7(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims shall define the matter for which protection is sought in terms of the technical features of the invention; they shall be clear and concise and be supported by the description. The number of claims shall be reasonable, and where several, numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should balance completeness and concision; 'reasonable' depends on nature of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-part claim structure where appropriate (Rule 7(1)(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, claims shall contain (a) a statement indicating technical features necessary for definition but which, in combination, are part of the prior art; and (b) a characterizing portion—preceded by words such as 'characterized in that', 'characterized by', 'wherein the improvement comprises'—stating concisely the technical features which with (a) are desired to be protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of standard transitional/characterizing language recommended for clarity of novel contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must not rely on references to description or drawings (Rule 7(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall not, except where absolutely necessary, rely, in respect of technical features, on references to the description or drawings; in particular avoid references such as 'as described in part ...' or 'as illustrated in figure ...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should be self-contained; reliance on description/drawings weakens claim clarity and may be objected to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard phrasing for medical indication/use claims (Rule 7(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims related to medical indications or use claims shall, for examination, be drafted in accordance with the standard phrases provided (list of first medical indications: e.g., 'Pharmaceutical composition for the prophylaxis/treatment of Y comprising X', 'Compound X for use as a drug/medicament for the treatment of Y', 'Use of X for preparing a medicament', etc.; and second medical indications: e.g., 'Use of X for the manufacture/preparation of a medicament for the treatment of Y', 'Process for the preparation of a medicament ... characterized in that compound X is used as the main active component').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow provided formulations to ensure acceptability in examination of medical use claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim formalities and multiple dependent claims (Rule 7(4)(a)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent claim including all features of one or more other claims shall do so by a reference (if possible at the beginning) to the other claim(s) and then state the additional features. Multiple dependent claims must refer to the claims in the alternative only and shall not serve as a basis for any other multiple dependent claims. Claims shall be grouped logically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent-claim structure must be clear; multiple-dependence restricted to alternative references and cannot chain multiple-dependent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention requirement for groups of inventions (Rule 7(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A group of inventions claimed in an ARIPO application meets unity only when there is a technical relationship involving one or more of the same or corresponding 'special technical features'—those features which define a contribution each claimed invention makes over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity is assessed on contribution over prior art, not merely claim format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial search/examination and divisional remedy for lack of unity (Rule 7(5)(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office considers the application lacks unity, it shall draw up a partial search/examination report on the invention first mentioned in the claims, inform applicant that search/examination opinion covers only that subject-matter, invite limitation to that invention, and advise that remaining inventions can be filed as divisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may file divisionals to pursue non-first inventions; expect partial coverage in search/exam reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity determination independent of claim format (Rule 7(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination whether a group of inventions is so linked as to form a single general inventive concept shall be made without regard to whether the inventions are claimed in separate claims or as alternatives within a single claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple independent claims in same category allowed only in listed cases (Rule 7(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO application may contain more than one independent claim in the same category only if the subject-matter involves: (a) a plurality of interrelated products; (b) different uses of a product or apparatus; or (c) alternative solutions to a particular problem where inappropriate to cover by a single claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reference signs in claims (Rule 7(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where drawings include reference signs, technical features in the claims shall preferably be followed by such reference signs in parentheses if intelligibility is increased; these reference signs shall not be construed as limiting the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference numerals may aid clarity but are non-limiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biotechnology definitions (Rule 7bis.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines terms used in biotech guidelines: 'biological material', 'microbiological process', 'biotechnological invention', 'genetic engineering', 'plant variety', and 'essentially biological process'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions set scope for what is considered biotech subject-matter under subsequent rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability of biotechnological inventions (Rule 7bis.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Biotechnological inventions shall be patentable if they concern (i) 'biological material' isolated from its natural environment or produced by a technical process even if it previously occurred in nature; (ii) 'plants or animals' provided technical feasibility is not confined to a particular plant or animal variety; (iii) 'a microbiological or other technical process,' or a product obtained by such a process other than a plant or animal variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentability hinges on isolation/technical production and general technical feasibility beyond a single variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to patentability of biotechnological inventions (Rule 7bis.3(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO patents shall not be granted for biotechnological inventions concerning processes for cloning human beings; processes for modifying germ line genetic identity of humans; uses of human embryos for industrial or commercial purposes; processes modifying genetic identity of animals likely to cause suffering without substantial medical benefit and resulting animals; embryonic stem cells/animals at various formation stages belong to animal variety; a single plant and its reproductive material belong to plant variety; inventions lacking practical applicability; the human body at various stages and mere discovery of its elements (including gene sequences) are not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive list of excluded biotech subject-matter — practical applicability and ethical limits enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plants/animals from essentially biological processes excluded (Rule 7bis.3(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Section 3(10)(j)(ii), ARIPO patents shall not be granted in respect of plants or animals exclusively obtained by means of an essentially biological process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of declaration of priority (Rule 8(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration claiming priority shall indicate: (i) the date of the earlier application; (ii) the number of the earlier application (subject to Rule 8(2)); (iii) the name of the State in which the earlier application was filed or, for regional/international applications, the State(s) for which it was filed; (iv) where regional/international, the office with which it was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaration should identify earlier filing precisely to claim Paris Convention priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for making declaration of priority (Rule 8(2)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration preferably on filing; may be made within 16 months from earliest priority date for patents/utility models and 10 months for industrial designs. If earlier application number unknown at filing, it must be furnished within 3 months. Corrections to declaration may be made within 16 months (or 10 months for designs) subject to earlier deadlines specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict timing; corrections permitted but limited by 16-/10-month windows and related filing/translation deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents to support priority claim (Rule 8(5)-(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant shall, within 3 months from filing of the application containing the declaration, furnish a certified copy of the earlier application; if in a language other than English, furnish an English translation within 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply means declaration is disregarded (Rule 8(7)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application content for industrial designs (Rule 9(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for an industrial design shall contain: (a) a request; (b) a reproduction of the industrial design; (c) a designation of the Contracting States for registration; and be subject to payment of prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules relating to patent applications apply mutatis mutandis to industrial designs per Rule 9(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application rules for utility models (Rule 9bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules relating to patent applications, particularly Rules 5 to 8 and 19bis, shall, mutatis mutandis, apply to applications for registration of utility models filed under Section 3ter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to file and representative authorization (Rule 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application may be filed with either the Office or the industrial property office of any Contracting State. Authorization of the applicant's representative shall be evidenced by a power of attorney filed with the application or within 2 months after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing of power of attorney required to evidence representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees: schedule, currency and undertakings (Rule 11(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees and amounts are set out in the Schedule of Fees and Administrative Instructions. Fees shall be paid in U.S. dollars direct to the Office or the application accompanied by an undertaking to pay within 21 days. Where applicant is a national of the Contracting State in which filed, that office may accept local currency equivalent and request the Office to debit its ARIPO account; the Office is bound by the industrial property office's decision on this applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment or undertaking required; nationals may pay locally subject to local office's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional fee for pages and claims fee (Rule 11bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional fee is payable for ARIPO patent applications comprising more than 30 pages (calculated per Schedule of Fees). Pages forming part of a sequence listing complying with WIPO ST.25 are not counted. Any application with more than 10 claims incurs a claims fee for the 11th and subsequent claims. Fees must be paid on or before filing the request for substantive examination; non-payment leads to withdrawal or claims deemed withdrawn. Amendments after payment that introduce more pages/claims require further fees payable at grant/publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count pages carefully; pay additional/claims fees before requesting substantive examination to avoid withdrawal/claim loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of fees between Office and Contracting States (Rule 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution: (a) 5% of application fees due to Contracting State where filed and 95% to the Office; (b) 50% of designation fee to each designated State and 50% to the Office; (c) 50% of annual maintenance fee to designated State and 50% to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting States may request transmission of fees due to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal duties of industrial property office (Rule 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where application filed with a Contracting State office, that office shall verify the application fulfills Rule 5(1)(a)-(c), verify fee undertaking or payment, mark documents with receipt date/number/stamp, issue acknowledgement to applicant's representative, and promptly transmit all documents to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local offices serve as intake and forwarding points; must check formal face-of-it requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date accorded when face-of-it requirements met (Rule 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office accords as the filing date the date on which the application was received by the Office or industrial property office provided the application on the face of it fulfills Rule 5(1)(a),(b),(c); if it did not at receipt, the filing date is the date on which it on the face of it fulfilled those requirements. The Office shall notify applicant and the industrial property office of each designated State of the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing date depends on face-of-it compliance at receipt or later correction date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination for formal requirements and invitation to correct (Rule 15(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving the application, the Office examines compliance with Section 3(1), 3ter(3) and 4(1), Rules 5, 6, 6bis, 7, 8, 10 and 11, Administrative Instructions and fee payment. If non-compliant, the Office invites the applicant to correct within 2 months. Failure to comply and subsequent refusal allows the applicant to request reconsideration in writing within 2 months stating grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict 2-month correction window; reconsideration requests must be timely and reasoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for reconsideration and appeals (Rule 15bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prescribed period for requesting reconsideration under Section 3(4) shall be not less than 2 months and not more than 6 months after notification of refusal. The applicant may lodge an appeal against Office decisions to the Board of Appeal within 3 months after notification of the Office decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the 2–6 month and 3-month appeal windows precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time limits (Rule 15ter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General may extend a time limit if (a) applicant requests it; (b) the request complies with relevant rules; or (c) due to exceptional occurrences (pandemic, natural disaster, war, civil disorder, general electronic communications breakdown). Multiple extension requests in one application require payment of prescribed fee. Extension shall not exceed 3 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions limited to 3 months and require compliance and fees where multiple.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to furnish information on corresponding foreign applications (Rule 16(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: At the Office's request and within the specified period the applicant shall furnish date and number of any foreign application relating to same or essentially same invention. For one foreign application the applicant must provide copies of communications on search/examination results, copies of patents or final rejection decisions, and any final decisions invalidating the patent. For other foreign applications, provide communications mentioning prior art publications or final decisions rejecting/refusing grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents facilitate evaluation of novelty and inventive step; applicant may submit comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal and change in designated States (Rule 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may withdraw an application at any time by written declaration. Applicant may reduce number of designated States at any time subject to prescribed fee. For ARIPO applications, applicant may add designated States any time before publication subject to Rule 8, by written request; the request is deemed filed when request fee, designation fee and any outstanding maintenance fee for added States have been lodged. The period for adding is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding designations requires timely payment of fees; reductions permitted with fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination: timing and consequences (Rule 18(1)-(1)(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may request substantive examination up to 3 years from filing or priority date (earliest if multiple). For divisional applications the limit is 6 months from lodging. The request is deemed filed when request fee (including additional and claims fees if any) has been lodged. If no request made within prescribed period the application shall be deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to the 3-year/6-month deadlines and fee lodging to keep applications pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and examination reports and communication of objections (Rule 18(2)-(3)(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A search report and examination report shall be established and contain conclusions. If Office concludes requirements in Section 3(3) are not fulfilled, it shall notify applicant attaching the reports and invite observations and amended application within a period specified in the Administrative Instructions, and may request a reconsideration under Section 3(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports form basis for objections; applicant must respond within set Administrative Instruction periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary amendments during examination (Rule 18(3)(b)(i)-(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary amendments before search/exam report is communicated are not subject to these provisions. With each response to an office action raising objections the applicant may amend description, claims and drawings. Each amendment may only be incorporated through a written examination report consenting to such amendments. Applicant must identify amendments and indicate basis in the disclosure as filed; Office may request correction within 2 months if deficiency noted. Amended claims may not relate to unsearched subject-matter that does not combine with the original invention to form a single general inventive concept. Introduction of unsearched/unexamined claims may be allowable subject to payment of new search/examination fees. Voluntary amendments after an application has been recommended for grant are considered under Section 5ter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are tightly controlled: basis identification, consent by office, and fees for unsearched subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant communication and payment of grant/publication fee (Rule 18(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Office decides to grant the patent, it shall notify the applicant attaching the search and examination report and request payment of grant and publication fee within the period it specifies. The Office shall communicate the decision to applicant, industrial property office and make it available to public in each designated State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated State communications and response timelines (Rule 18(5)-(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: A communication by a designated State under Section 3(6) is made by its industrial property office. If a designated State communicates the patent shall have no effect in its territory, the applicant may respond within 3 months; the designated State shall respond within 3 months of receipt of applicant's communication. The Office shall transmit copies of such communications to the applicant within 2 weeks of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely bilateral communications between applicant and designated States required; Office acts as conduit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification of examination timeline: expedited and delayed options (Rule 18(7)(a)-(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may request preferential substantive examination with a modified timeframe: (a) Expedited/Accelerated Examination to have decision within a period specified in Administrative Instructions, subject to: single invention or applicant agrees examining division considers only first identified invention; applicant undertakes to respond immediately to clarifications; application being withdrawn and then reinstated before conclusion of examination; and a search report based on acceptable minimum documentation on claims of same or narrower scope is availed. (b) Delayed commencement of substantive examination up to 1 year beyond Rule 18(1)(a) provided a request for substantive examination has been lodged in time, a written explanation satisfactory to Director General submitted, and application not deemed withdrawn due to non-payment of annuities. (c) Office will acknowledge requests and direct applicant to remit fees or confirm concurrence if relates to green technologies or indicate impossibility with reasons. (d) Requests not considered made unless prescribed fees paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions for expedited/delayed handling are strict (single invention, immediate responses, supporting search reports, fees); green technology may receive special confirmation per Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application formalities (Rule 18bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may file a divisional relating to any pending earlier ARIPO application. Divisional must be filed in the language of the proceedings for the earlier application; if earlier was not in an official language of the Office, divisional may be filed in the language of the earlier application but a translation into the language of the proceedings must be filed within 2 months. Divisional is filed with the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language and filing-place rules for divisionals are mandatory; watch 2-month translation window when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model substantive examination limitations and timeline modifications (Rule 18ter)
rubrics_metrics.description: No utility model may be protected if it has already been the subject of a patent or registration based on a prior application or priority. Novelty and industrial applicability within Contracting States apply. Applicant may request expedited/delayed examination similar to Rule 18, subject to analogous conditions and fee payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility model protection excludes subject-matter already covered by patents/utility models; procedural options mirror patent rules but with utility-model-specific constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design substantive examination (Rule 18quater)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination of industrial designs shall be conducted in accordance with the national laws of each designated State. Communications by designated States under Section 4(3) shall be made by their industrial property offices. Where a designated State communicates that a registration shall have no effect in its territory, the applicant may respond within 3 months and the designated State shall respond within 3 months of receipt of the applicant's communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive grounds for designs are determined by national law of designated States; standard 3-month bilateral response windows apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for conversion into national application (Rule 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request that the ARIPO application be treated as an application under the national law of one or more designated States may be filed within 3 months from the date of refusal by the Office of the request for reconsideration and shall specify the designated States desired. Within 2 weeks of receiving the request the Office shall transmit copies of the application and all relevant documents to the industrial property offices of the designated States specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion requests are time-limited (3 months after reconsideration refusal) and trigger rapid transmission to national offices.
